               <ns0:p n="14">14 And profited in the Jews religion above many, my <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Gr. <ns0:hi>equals in years.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> equals in my own nation <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">The word here used and Translated <ns0:hi>profited,</ns0:hi> may be in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />terpreted either of his own personal proficiency, and go<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ng on in the <ns0:hi>Iewish</ns0:hi> Religion, or of his propagating of it, and ma<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />king that to go on, which seemeth to be the sense of the same word, 2 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 2.16. And it is observed, that Active Verbs in the <ns0:hi>Gr.</ns0:hi> in imitation of the <ns0:hi>Heb. Con. Pi<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>il.</ns0:hi> sometimes signifie to do ones self an action, sometimes to make others to do it; and <ns0:hi>Pauls</ns0:hi> wasting the Christian Church had a rational tenden<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cy to uphold and propagate <ns0:hi>Iudaism,</ns0:hi> the propagation of which was the end designed by it; this he saith he did, <ns0:hi>above others of his countrymen, that were his equals</ns0:hi> in years. By this also he lets them know, that his persecuting the Christian Church was not a passionate act, or for a gain to himself, but from an er<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />roneous judgment, he verily thought that he ought to do wha<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> he did, against Jesus of <ns0:hi>Nazareth,</ns0:hi> and his Disciples.</ns0:note>, being more exceeding zealous of the traditions of my fathers <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">He ad<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />deth, <ns0:hi>that he was more exceedingly zealous of the Traditions of the Father</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> By which he understands not only the Rites of the <ns0:hi>Ce<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />remonial Law,</ns0:hi> but the whole body of their <ns0:hi>Constitutions,</ns0:hi> which the <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ulers of that Church had made, under the notion of <ns0:hi>sep<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>
                        <ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />menta Legis,</ns0:hi> hedges or fences to the Lawes of God; to keep men at a distance from the violation of them, and other con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stitutions also, of which they had innumerable. <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> was a <ns0:hi>Pharisee,</ns0:hi> (the Son of a <ns0:hi>Pharisee, Acts</ns0:hi> 23.6.) bred up at the feet of <ns0:hi>Gamaliel</ns0:hi>; (one of the Doctors of their Law) this was the strictest Sect (for Ceremonies) of their Religion; and this his zeal for Traditions, is that which he calleth a progress, or profiting in the <ns0:hi>Iewish</ns0:hi> Religion, and was a cause of the pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pagation of that Religion.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="15">15 But when it pleased God <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Rom. 1.<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
                  </ns0:note> who separated me from my mothers womb <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">Here are two acts predicated of God, with relation to <ns0:hi>Paul,</ns0:hi> the first is a <ns0:hi>separating of him from the womb</ns0:hi>; the same was said of two of the great Prophets, <ns0:hi>Isaiah</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Ieremiah, Isa.</ns0:hi> 49.1. <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 1.5. The Apostle here is not speaking of Gods decree, predestinating him to Eternal Life, but of his determining him to the work of an Apostle. God predetermineth men to the stations they shall take up in the World; especially such who are to take up stations, wherein they are to be eminently use<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ful and serviceable to him.</ns0:note>, and called <ns0:hi>me</ns0:hi> by his grace <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">The second act predicated of God is his <ns0:hi>calling of Paul</ns0:hi>; This is an act in time, and lyeth much in the preparing of persons for the work allotted to them, and in inclining the heart to it. Thus God called <ns0:hi>Paul,</ns0:hi> fitting him for the work of the Ministry, and inclining him to it<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> to which he added his immediate command from Hea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ven, that he should go and preach the Gospel. Both these acts of God are ascribed to his good pleasure, and grace, no<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thing but his meer free love, and favour moving him, either to separate, or to call <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> to this high and great employment.</ns0:note>,</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="16">16 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">2 Cor. 4.6.</ns0:note> To reveal his Son in me, that <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Eph. 3.8.</ns0:note> I might preach him among the heathen <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">When it pleased God to discover Christ his Son (by an Eternal Generation) to me, whom neither naturally, nor from any instruction in my Education, was acquainted with any thing of Christ; but according to the common prejudices of those of my own Country, looked upon him as a meer man, and an Impostor; and also revealed to me the end of that dis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />covery, not only that I my self should receive and embrace him, but that I should publish him amongst the Heathens, (where he intimates the specialty of his Separation and call); I (saith he) immediately advised with no mortal man living, (for that is signified by Flesh and Blood, <ns0:hi>Mat.</ns0:hi> 16.17. 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 15.50.) but resolved with my self to address my self to that work and employment to which I had such a special call from God.</ns0:note>, immediately I conferred not with flesh and blood <ns0:hi>b.</ns0:hi>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="17">17 Neither went I up to Jerusalem, to them that were apostles before me <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">As <ns0:hi>Ierusalem</ns0:hi> was the place for the Oracle of the Law, un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />der the Old Testament; so it also was for the Gospel upon the first publication of it. There the Disciples were, they return<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed thither after they had seen Christ ascend to Heaven, <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 24.52. from thence they were not to depart, but to wait <ns0:hi>there for the promise of the Father, Acts</ns0:hi> 1.4. There the Holy Ghost came down upon them, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 2. there they continued till the persecution scattered them; there was the Colledge of the Apostles. <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> saith that upon his Conversion, he did not go up thither, nor till <ns0:hi>three years after,</ns0:hi> (as he tells us in the next verse); but he</ns0:note>, but I went in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />to Arabia <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">went into <ns0:hi>Arabia,</ns0:hi> amongst the Heathens, and the most wild and barbarous Heathens, (for such were the <ns0:hi>Arabians.</ns0:hi>) <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> in the <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> tells us nothing of this. From hence it was easie to conclude, that <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> had not his Commis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sion from the other Apostles that were before him, for he saw none of them till he had been a preacher of the Gospel to the wild <ns0:hi>Arabians</ns0:hi> three years.</ns0:note>, and returned again unto Damas<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cus <ns0:hi>e.</ns0:hi>
                  <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">And then he returned to <ns0:hi>Damas<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cus</ns0:hi>; the word is <ns0:gap reason="foreign">

                     </ns0:gap>, which is by some observed to signi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fie his being compelled to return, (as they judge) by some persecution raised amongst the Heathens; but of this the Scrip<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ture saith nothing.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:476" />18 Then after three years, I <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>I returned.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> went up to Je<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rusalem to see Peter, and abode with him fifteen dayes <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">These three years were spent partly in <ns0:hi>Arabia,</ns0:hi> partly <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">

                     </ns0:gap> 
                     <ns0:hi>Damascus,</ns0:hi> whither he returned; and his being there, was not idle, but as <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> informes us, preached Christ in the Syna<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gogues, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 9.20, 22, 26. <ns0:hi>confounded the Iewes, proving that this was the very Christ,</ns0:hi> which made the <ns0:hi>Iewes</ns0:hi> take counsel to kill him: Here it was that he escaped them, by being let down over the wall in a basket. Upon another journey which <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> made to <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> he saw others, (as we shall hear in the next chapter); but that was several years after this his first journey thither.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="20">20 Now the things which I write unto you, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Rom. 9.1.</ns0:note> behold, before God I lie not <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">Whether those words [<ns0:hi>before God</ns0:hi>] make this sentence an Oath, is not material to determine, they are either an Oath, or a very serious Asseveration. If the Apostle designed to call God for a witness, to the correspondence of his words, with the truth of the things he had spoken, they make up an asser<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tory Oath, which was lawful enough (though privately taken) in so serious a matter as this, where the Apostle is vindicating his <ns0:hi>Apostleship</ns0:hi>; from some Acts of which probably he had no Witnesses at hand to produce; but they may be understood (by the supplement of, <ns0:hi>I speak,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>I say this</ns0:hi>) only as a form of serious assertion, to confirm the truth of what he asserted. He minds them, that he was sensible of Gods presence in all places, and particular taking notice of the things spoken; as being spoken before him, who knew that what he spake was truth.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="21">21 Afterwards I came into the regions of Sy<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ria, and Cilicia <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">After that I came from <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> I came into the Country of <ns0:hi>Syria,</ns0:hi> probably not to <ns0:hi>Damascus,</ns0:hi> the chief City of <ns0:hi>Syria,</ns0:hi> (where he had so narrow an escape in a basket) but into the Country parts of <ns0:hi>Syria</ns0:hi>; (for <ns0:hi>Syria</ns0:hi> lay in the way betwixt <ns0:hi>Iudea</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Cilicia.</ns0:hi>) It appeareth by <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 9.30. that <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> was de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />signed for <ns0:hi>Tarsus,</ns0:hi> his Native place; where we are also told, that the Brethren conducted him to <ns0:hi>Cesarea,</ns0:hi> which stood upon the confines of <ns0:hi>Syria.</ns0:hi> It is probable that he stayed some time at <ns0:hi>Tarsus</ns0:hi>; for there <ns0:hi>Barnabas</ns0:hi> found him, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 11.25, 26. <ns0:hi>and brought him to Antioch</ns0:hi>; so that <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> had but fifteen dayes at <ns0:hi>Ierusalem</ns0:hi> to converse with the Apostles, and in that time he saw none of them, but <ns0:hi>Peter,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iames</ns0:hi> the Son of <ns0:hi>Alpheus.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="22">22 And was unknown by face unto the churches of Judea, which were in Christ <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">

In this sense the Apostle saith, <ns0:hi>if any man be in Christ he is a new creature.</ns0:hi> 2. Their being <ns0:hi>Christians</ns0:hi> in name, by <ns0:hi>Baptism</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>outward pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fession.</ns0:hi> These Churches are said to be in Christ in this latter sense. We have a parallel Text, 1 <ns0:hi>Thess.</ns0:hi> 2.14 They do not judge improperly, who think that by <ns0:hi>Iudea</ns0:hi> here, is not meant the <ns0:hi>Province,</ns0:hi> but the whole Country of <ns0:hi>Iudea</ns0:hi>; which com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />prehended not <ns0:hi>Iudea</ns0:hi> only, but <ns0:hi>Samaria</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Galilee. Of all these Churches <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> speaks; telling us, he was personally unknown unto them. So far he was from learning the Christian Doctrine from the Apostles, or them.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
